stt: Ask HN: Books you read in 2015?
x:
"Leaving Orbit - Notes from the last days of American spaceflight" - pleasantly sentimental view of the wind down of the shuttle program.

"The Dark Forest" 2nd installment in Three Body Problem series. Quite clever.

"This Changes Everything" - triggered by a quote from the doc on the radio about trying not to think about climate change and whether it's possible to be bored by the end of the world. Lots of good info (including a visit to a climate deniers conference), bit long winded.

"The Princeton Companion to Applied Mathematics". If I read only 10% still worth it. Lots of things to dip into.

"The Astronomer and the Witch" Kepler fights to save his mother from persecution.

stt: Ask HN: What good books have you read in 2016?
x:
"This changes everything" by Naomi Klein. It's a very well-written, liberal book on climate policy failures written by an investigative journalist.

I think it was written in 2014, so it doesn't cover the latest trends in fracking or solar. I didn't know anything about the climate industry coming from a silicon valley background, so this was an ingestible yet detailed primer.

stt: Investing Prophet Jeremy Grantham Takes Aim at Climate Change
x:
It's definitely the case that Capital will profit--in the short term, of course--from climate change, and there's a good argument to be made that Capital is perpetuating the cataclysmic destruction of our system for such profits.

Check out [This Changes Everything](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/21913812-this-changes-ev...).

stt: Climate talks break up with no agreement on carbon trading
x:
This is the thesis of Naomi Klein books. Current political system and pseudo-market solutions are incapable of solving the climate problem. And so far, unfortunately it is proven right.

I do agree in principle (with some reservations perhaps).

[] https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/21913812-this-changes-ev...
